newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares open slightly higher in light trade.
newsitem.headline: French shares open slightly higher in light trade.

text.p: French shares opened slightly higher in light trading on Friday as many investors were on an extended weekend holiday following May Day and ahead of a key U.S. economic indicator due this afternoon.
The April unemployment figure is expected at 1230 GMT with economists expecting the unemployment rate to stay unchanged at 5.2 percent.
The CAC-40 index opened 0.25 percent higher at 2,646.05 and at 0805 GMT it was 0.39 percent higher at 2,649.68.
The British election victory for Labour is not expected to affect the French parliamentary election outlook, dealers said.
An IPSOS opinion poll for the weekly Le Point credited the centre-right with 40.5 percent of the vote, the leftist alliance 38 percent, and the National Front 15.5 percent.
Translated into seats, the poll carried out on April 29 and 30 among 1,620 people gave 331 to the centre-right, 245 to the left, and one seat to the Front.

Rhone-Poulenc added another 1.38 percent to 199 francs after a big gain on Wednesday on a 6.5 percent first quarter net income rise and forecast for a 20 percent rise in 1997 earnings per share before exceptionals.
Agence Havas, up 2.29 percent at 447 francs, extended Wednesday's gains on the back of a road show in Geneva.
French bonds were also higher as a big U.S. fund kept buying paper.
Stock volume was a low 490 million francs.
Computer firm Bull traded eight percent lower at 45.65 francs after the state placed 17 million shares at prices of 36 and 38 francs. Bull had been suspended since April 11.
